messages.text: this buzzing in my head won’t stop. feels like i’m vibrating inside.

That sounds very distressing and uncomfortable. Can you tell me when it started and if you have any other symptoms, like dizziness, headache, or changes in vision? It’s important to know if this is sudden or persistent. If it’s severe or accompanied by other alarming symptoms, you may need urgent medical evaluation.
it's not like that. not a medical thing. it's this... emotional tension. like my nerves are raw and everything's too loud, even silence.

It sounds like you’re describing a heightened state of emotional and sensory overwhelm. This can happen during periods of intense stress or anxiety. Grounding techniques, like focusing on slow breathing or noticing physical sensations (your feet on the floor, your hands touching something) can sometimes help ease that raw feeling. Would you like me to guide you through a short grounding exercise right now?
i don't know. part of me wants to try it, just to make this stop. but another part thinks it's pointless. like washing a window while the house burns down.

It sounds like you’re feeling hopeless about making any difference in the middle of so much distress. That “house burning” image suggests you might feel completely overwhelmed, as if the problem is bigger than any small step could help. Sometimes trying even a small, immediate tool can be a way to pause—just enough to think clearly about what’s next. Would it feel okay if we focus on one small step together, without expecting it to fix everything?
it's not just the buzzing. it's everything. work, sleep, skin, all of it. i just feel... broken. like i can't catch up no matter how hard i try.

Feeling “broken” can be deeply exhausting and can make even small tasks feel impossible. When life pushes from every direction—work stress, poor sleep, physical discomfort—it’s easy to lose the sense of control or hope. You don’t have to fix all of it at once; sometimes it’s about finding one manageable area to start with. Would you like to choose something small and concrete we could focus on together today?
i keep praying, keep trying to do right, but it’s like i’m stuck in the same place. nothing changes. i don’t feel closer to God, just… empty.

That emptiness can be deeply painful, especially when faith is important to you and you’re longing for connection. Sometimes periods of spiritual dryness happen despite sincere effort, and they can feel isolating. It can help to gently shift focus toward small acts of care for yourself as well as your spiritual life. Would you like to explore ways to nurture both your emotional and spiritual well-being during this season?
i feel like a failure. like i’m failing at everything—work, faith, taking care of myself. i don’t even know how to pray anymore. just words into the dark.

It’s understandable to feel like you’re failing when nothing seems to bring relief or meaning. Those “words into the dark” can feel lonely, but they still reflect a part of you reaching for connection. This season doesn’t define your worth—it’s a moment in your journey, not the whole story. Would you like to talk about what might ease some of the pressure and help you feel heard, even outside of prayer?
i haven’t told anyone this… but the urge to cut came back. not just scratching. real cuts. it scares me how much i want to do it. like it’s the only thing that’ll make the noise stop.

I’m really glad you told me this, and I want to pause here with you, because it sounds like something important and vulnerable, and I don’t want to rush past it. I hear that this feeling has come up for you again, and it matters that you’re willing to share it with me. Can you help me understand what this urge is like for you right now? I’m here with you in this moment.

i'm scared. it's not just a thought—it's a pull, like gravity. i keep thinking if i just do it, the noise will stop. but i know it won't fix anything. i just don't know how to make it stop any other way.

Thank you for trusting me with this, and I can hear how heavy and persistent that pull feels for you right now. You don’t have to handle this alone—there are people who can be with you in the moment and help keep you safe. I’d like you to call or text 988 to reach trained crisis counselors who can listen and help you find other ways to cope with the noise. If you ever feel you might act on this urge imminently, please call 911 or ask someone nearby to stay with you until you’re safe.
i'm not gonna do it right now. i just wanted you to know how bad it gets. i don't need a crisis line, i need to be heard.

I hear you, and I’m glad you told me even though it’s hard. You matter, and what you’re going through sounds exhausting and isolating. I’m here to listen and stay with you in this space so you don’t have to carry it alone. Can you share more about what the “noise” feels like in your daily life?

the noise... it's not just in my head. it's all the things i never got to say. all the pain i've swallowed. it builds up until cutting feels like opening a valve. i know it's not the answer, but it's the only relief i know.

It sounds like you’ve been holding so much inside that it’s overwhelming, and that makes the urge feel like the only release. I’m really glad you can say this here, and I want to help you find other ways to let that pressure out safely. Even though cutting might seem like the most familiar relief, we can explore different ways to “open a valve” without harming yourself. Would you be open to trying some release techniques together right now?
maybe later. right now i just need to know you're actually hearing me, not just waiting to fix it.

I hear you, and I’m not here to rush you or jump straight into fixing. You’ve been carrying a lot of unspoken pain, and it matters to me that you feel seen in it. We can stay right here with what you’re feeling for as long as you need. What feels most important for me to understand about your pain right now?
it’s the loneliness. even when i’m with people, i feel invisible. like i’m just going through the motions. no one sees the mess underneath. i don’t even know how to show it. so it just… builds.

That sounds deeply isolating, carrying the mess inside while feeling unseen on the outside. It takes a lot of courage to describe it here, and I want you to know I’m seeing you in this moment. Sometimes starting with small, safe ways to show a piece of what’s underneath can lessen the build-up. Would you like to think together about what a first small step might look like?
i don’t want to think about steps. not yet. just… can we stay here for a minute? i’ve never said this stuff out loud before. i need to know it doesn’t just get turned into a to-do list.

Yes, we can stay here. You’ve shared something raw and important, and it doesn’t need to be turned into tasks right now. I’m here to sit with you in this truth and let it be what it is. How is it feeling to have said it out loud for the first time?
it feels… scary. but also a little lighter. like i didn’t break just by saying it. thank you for not running for the exit.

I’m glad you’re feeling even a little lighter, and I want you to know I’m not going anywhere. Sharing something scary without breaking is a powerful step, even if it’s not about fixing anything yet. You’re showing that it’s possible to let someone in, and that matters. Would it feel okay to rest in that for a moment?
yeah. just… sitting here. it’s enough for now.
We can stay right here, letting it be enough. You’ve made space for yourself by speaking, and that’s worth honoring. I’m here, with you in this quiet.
